extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of American political thought; reformers; political scientists; general educated public interested in democracy and reform
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts evaluative criteria and standards the author uses to judge the roles of lawyers and reformers in American democracy, and the social/political conditions that affect reform. Intended to guide assessment of legal-political actors and reform movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawyers as constitutional interpreters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court as the interpreter of the Fundamental Law made the American lawyer responsible for the future of the country; whenever its action can be legally invoked it can declare the will of either or both the President and Congress of no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lawyer consecrated as Justice of the Supreme Court is described as 'the High Priest of our political faith' who 'guards the sacred rights ... enshrined in the ark of the Constitution.' This elevates judicial construction to a constructive political function, not merely negative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of lawyers' qualifications for political guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The adequacy of the lawyers' training, the disinterestedness of their political motives, the fairness of their mental outlook, and the closeness of their contact with the national public opinion are matters of grave public concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These qualities are presented as necessary criteria for lawyers to perform their role legitimately; deficits increase the risk of false diagnoses of political problems and produce serious public consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representativeness of the legal profession and the Supreme Court
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court has been a success because the lawyers it represented were themselves representative of the ideas and interests of the bulk of their fellow-countrymen; if they become less representative, a dangerous division would be created between public opinion and its legal expositors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether judges and leading lawyers reflect 'the current of national political opinion'—lack of representativeness is a substantive failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency toward professional specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1870 lawyers have tended to become professional specialists, giving all their time to their specialty and less likely to become legislators and statesmen; the most eminent lawyers usually remain lawyers all their lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialization is a criterion that reduces the political experience and breadth of outlook expected of public-minded lawyers; assess whether a lawyer's specialization limits their capacity for public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of corporate retainers and special interests on lawyers' outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: The ablest American lawyers have been retained by special interests, and such retainers inevitably increase a blind conservatism and reduce contribution to essential political and legal reconstruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess conflicts of interest and corporate ties as indicators of conservatism and of failure to promote the public interest; corporate retainers are an explicit anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawyers' conservative bias vis-à-vis political/economic reorganization
rubrics_metrics.description: The tendency of the legally trained mind is inevitably and extremely conservative; while enforcement of the law is supported, political or economic reorganization faces opposition from much of American legal opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conservatism as a metric when judging lawyers' responsiveness to needed reorganization; conservative legal attitudes may impede reform beyond mere law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of constructive judicial decisions provoking crises
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Supreme Court misdiagnoses a serious political problem and attempts to settle it by decision (as in the Dred Scott example), such decisions would merely excite a crisis rather than allay it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate judicial remedies for deep social-political issues cautiously; judicial construction without broader consensus can exacerbate conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reformers' need for permanent organization and positive programme
rubrics_metrics.description: Reformers found the need of permanent organization, of constant work, and even within limits, of a positive programme; their influence increased as they took their job seriously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reform movements by organizational permanence, sustained activity, and presence of an articulated programme rather than by spasmodic protest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and cooperative 'team play' among reformers
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of 'team play' among reformers—preference for leading roles and 'stars'—has diminished the efficiency of reform as a political agitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure reform effectiveness by degree of cooperation and ability to subordinate individual star ambitions for collective strategy; factionalism is a failure mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify what 'reform' means in each movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform is an ambiguous catchword applied to many separate political agitations; different reformers mean very different things by the 'traditional system' they seek to restore (spiritual revival, strict law enforcement, new legal expression, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key evaluative criterion is conceptual clarity: assess whether a reformer/movement defines its conception of reform concretely and consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-partisanship as an unrealistic ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Reformers have tended to believe their agitation ought to be non-partisan, but in practice reform has rarely been non-partisan except in the minds of its more innocent advocates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge reform efforts on empirical partisanship and coalition-building rather than rhetorical claims of non-partisanship; expect partisan alignments and evaluate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local reform dependence on broader political reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Municipal reform often cannot be eradicated without reform of state politics and purging of local public service corporations; local non-partisan movements frequently enlarge and become partisan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate municipal reform proposals for their treatment of state-level and corporate-influence constraints; successful local reform often requires systemic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust and trust-busting remedies are often confused and contested
rubrics_metrics.description: The agitation against trusts has developed a confused hodge-podge of harmless and deadly, overlapping and mutually exclusive, remedies causing endless disagreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess antitrust proposals for internal coherence and clear linkage between diagnosis and remedy; multiplicity of conflicting remedies is a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform as moral and political purification (shared principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical reformers commonly agree to conceive of reform as at bottom a moral protest and awakening that seeks to enforce violated laws and restore political and economic system to pristine purity and vigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this shared moral-purification framing to evaluate rhetoric vs practical policy: determine whether a movement's measures amount to law enforcement only or to structural change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of a democratic social ideal to solve the social problem
rubrics_metrics.description: The solution of the social problem demands the substitution of a conscious social ideal for the earlier instinctive homogeneity of the American nation; solidarity must be restored by a democratic social ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proposed social policies by whether they articulate a constructive democratic social ideal that produces solidarity without sacrificing desirable individual and class distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition that social differentiation is not inherently evil but needs accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized organization and increasing discipline (engineers, artists, experts) indicate efficiency and emancipation but have perilous aspects because no sufficient provision has been made in the national democratic tradition for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reforms and social policies on whether they provide institutional accommodation for differentiated social groups rather than attempting to erase specialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform requires more than moral energy and minor legal changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevailing preconception that increases in moral energy plus minor legal changes will restore balance is 'less than half true' because abuses are tied to structural features of traditional institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure reform proposals by whether they address structural causes (institutional design, incentives, traditional constitutional arrangements) rather than relying solely on moral exhortation or small tweaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained vigilance and succession of reformers may be necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reformers tend to the opinion that a tradition of reform and succession of reformers will be demanded for vigilant protection of the American political and economic system against abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a movement recognizes the need for long-term institutional vigilance and succession planning, not just one-time victories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore solidarity by constructive ideal, not by reverting to past homogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: The solidarity to be restored must differ radically from earlier homogeneity; it should be a promise and constructive ideal giving consistency without sacrificing individual or class distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals claiming to 'restore' traditional conditions: prefer those that propose a forward-looking democratic ideal rather than attempts to revert to an earlier social sameness.
